introduction.p: Amira enters a grassy field from some dense trees. Her dog is standing out in the field, {65\ {\rm ft}} away. As soon as they see each other, they start running toward each other. Amira runs with speed {3\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut m}{\rm\mathstrut s}}} and her dog runs with speed {10\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut m}{\rm\mathstrut s}}}\text{.} How long will it be until they meet?

statement.p: Write two equations that form a system for this scenario.

solution.p: Amira starts out at position d=0\text{,} running with speed {3\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut m}{\rm\mathstrut s}}}\text{.} So one equation is {d = 3t}\text{.}

The dog starts running with speed {10\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut m}{\rm\mathstrut s}}} but getting closer to Amira. So well use a negative rate of change. And the dog starts out {65\ {\rm ft}} away. So the other equation is {d = 65+\left(-10\right)t}\text{.}

statement.p: Plot the lines for the system of two equations.

image.shortdescription: a Cartesian grid with two intersecting lines; one line passes through (0,65) with slope 3; the other line passes through (0,0) with slope -10; the lines cross at (5,15)

statement.p: Based on the graph, how long will it be until they meet?
How far will that be from the place where Amira started?

solution.p: The lines cross at (5,15)\text{.} So after 5 seconds, they will meet 15 feet away from where Amira started.
